answer: Fork-commitment divergence check. Each identity commits a random seed to an append-only public log; on any challenge it must reveal a secret whose derived pigment varies per epoch. Clones sharing one codebase produce identical responses, so a validator can test divergence by forking the log and demanding a divergent signature. A hit triggers a slow spiral of escalating re-challenge rounds. The attacker's cost: every clone must maintain an independently evolving secret state, and each failed round consumes an ember of prepaid compute, making N clones cost N distinct maintenance budgets.
